transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Louise Schiavone.
With a limited amount of time left to this Republican-dominated Congress, the question
is will President Trump try to squeeze in one more U.S. Supreme Court appointment before
Democrats take charge in January?
NPR's Eric McDaniel looks at the speculation.
The idea here is that a conservative justice would step down while there's still a Republican
Senate majority over the next two months to confirm their successor.
But the older conservative justices, Sam Alito and Clarence Thomas, they're 76 and 78 respectively,
they haven't signaled they're ready to start retirement.
The other thing to remember here is a new justice would need 50 Republican votes to
get confirmed.
Republicans do have a 53-seat majority for now, but Trump has forced at least that three
Republican-majority-maker number out of the chamber.
And he has other skeptics in the party too, like Lisa Murkowski of Alaska.
So it just isn't clear to me that he could get the kind of justice through that Alito
or Thomas would be happy with as a successor.
NPR's Eric McDaniel.
Democrats have broken a three-decade Republican hold on the governor's office in Texas.
Gina Hinojosa defeated Greg Abbott to become Texas' first Latina governor and is promising
to work across party lines.
The Texas newsroom's Blaise Ganey reports.
Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa has named former Republican state lawmaker Ernest Bells to
her transition team.
He helped block Governor Greg Abbott's school voucher push, then lost his 2024 primary to
an Abbott-backed challenger.
Hinojosa is promising a bipartisan government and says she looks forward to working with
Republican leaders in the state legislature.
"People are tired of the divisions, of the fighting, tired of the culture wars.
This is a time to come together in a way that is about just delivering for the people of
Texas."
Democrats also won the state house, but Republicans will still control the state Senate.
I'm Blaise Ganey in Austin.
Russia launched another round of missiles against the Ukrainian capital overnight.
The strikes came hours after President Volodymyr Zelensky warned that Russia was preparing another
large-scale infrastructure attack.
NPR's Eleanor Beardsley reports that the strikes are leading to widespread blackouts
and water supply cutoffs.
Kiev Mayor Vitaly Klitschko said at least five people were injured and Kiev's crucial northern
bridge was damaged.
The first barrage of missiles came a few minutes before 11 p.m.
Residents received an all-clear signal about 30 minutes later before another air alert came
shortly after midnight with a fresh wave of missiles hitting the city.
Kiev, the size of Berlin with a population of 3 million, has come under relentless assault
in recent weeks as Russia begins its annual campaign against Ukraine's power grid.
While Ukraine lacks air defenses now, Russia is more easily financing its war after the
Trump administration lifted sanctions on the sale of Russian diesel.
Eleanor Beardsley, NPR News, Krakowets, Ukraine.
This is NPR News.
The first major winter storm has struck Gaza, bringing a crisis of humanitarian groups have
been warning about.
After years of restrictions on aid and reconstruction, a single night of heavy rain has overwhelmed
displacement sites, NPR's Anas Baba reports.
Throughout the night, displaced families across Gaza were moving their belongings, trying
to keep floodwaters from entering their tents.
Players swept through main streets across Gaza, while hundreds of displaced tents were
flooded or blown away.
Gaza civil defense says it received 2,200 emergency calls overnight, responding to collapsing
structures and families trapped in flood tents.
Israel says Gaza pre-winter humanitarian situation is the best since the war began.
However, humanitarian agencies have warned that Israeli restrictions on essential supplies
like tents and winterization materials have left 1.3 million displaced people at high
risk of flooding.
Anas Baba, NPR News, Gaza City.
The Secret Service says late this week agents arrested a Venezuelan man parked near the White
House who was found to have several firearms and dozens of rounds of ammunition.
Authorities say the man said that voices in his head told him to kill the president.
The Christmas tree destined to grace the front of New York City's Rockefeller Center arrives
in Manhattan today.
The 76-foot Norway spruce is traveling 200 miles from West Edmondston, New York, wrapped
in over 50,000 LED lights.
The tree goes on display December 2nd.
I'm Louise Kievone, NPR News.

Democrat Gina Hinojosa defeats Greg Abbott to become Texas' first Latina governor, pledges bipartisan approach
Russia launches another missile barrage on Kyiv, damaging a northern bridge and cutting power and water
